subject: Clarify BAA applicability for tokenized EHR snippets used in analytics
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@mediq-analytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: BAA question — tokenized EHR snippets + analytics

Hi Soojin,

Quick question as we're scoping an integration: our analytics pipeline needs to send short, tokenized EHR snippets to Redwood for real-time feature extraction and downstream aggregation. The tokenization we use replaces direct identifiers with stable tokens (SHA256 truncated) and we keep the mapping table inside our systems.

Two specific things we need clarified for procurement before we move forward:
- Under Redwood's policy, does sending these tokenized snippets to the Hosted API trigger BAA/PHI restrictions, or is the Hosted offering acceptable if we retain mapping and tokens are irreversible to Redwood?
- Do derived/aggregated outputs (counts, histograms, non-identifying feature vectors) ever get treated as PHI by Redwood if the mapping is retained by us?
- Are request/response logs persisted by default for Hosted, and can logging be disabled or limited for this integration?

I've attached a simple dataflow diagram (mediq-dataflow-v2.drawio.pdf) showing the point at which tokens are created and where we call Redwood. Can you advise whether we need Dedicated/Private to stay compliant, or whether Hosted + a BAA is sufficient?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call with Marcus or someone from infra if helpful.

—Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Engineering, MedIQ Analytics
alex.turner@mediq-analytics.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@mediq-analytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: BAA question — tokenized EHR snippets + analytics

Alex — thanks for the clear diagram and questions. Short answer: it depends on two things — (1) whether tokens are reversible by any party with access to Redwood systems, and (2) what retention/logging policies you need. A few clarifying points before I give a recommendation: 

1) Token reversibility: you said you keep the mapping table in your systems and tokens are SHA256-truncated. Can you confirm that no mapping or re-identification keys are ever transmitted to Redwood (even in troubleshooting payloads)?

2) Use of outputs: will any of the derived outputs you get back from Redwood be re-joined with identifiers on your side, or are they only used as anonymous metrics?

3) Fine-tuning / data reuse: do you plan to have Redwood use any incoming payloads for model fine-tuning, embeddings index, or quality monitoring? We treat fine-tuning data and dev/ops logs differently from ephemeral generation requests.

For context on Redwood controls:
- Hosted API: request/response payloads are transmitted and (by default) retained in operational logs for troubleshooting/quality for a configurable retention window (default 30 days). Hosted does not provide customer-managed KMS or network isolation.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, per-tenant isolation, and options to reduce retained telemetry; better fit when the workload contains PHI that customers cannot allow in shared environments.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full isolation, customer-managed KMS/HSM, and contract controls needed for regulated PHI workloads.

Prelim recommendation: if your tokens are truly irreversible to Redwood, and you do not send mapping keys or request that we reuse data for fine-tuning, Hosted + an executed BAA could be acceptable with additional configuration (reduced telemetry retention and disabled request-logging). However, we need to validate the tokenization scheme and your operational guarantees. If you need absolute separation or want to avoid any possibility of a re-identification path (including from combined analytics signals), Dedicated or Private is safer.

Next steps: can you share a redacted sample payload (hashed/tokenized) and confirm no plan to fine-tune? I can loop in Marcus from infra for questions on telemetry and Monica from Customer Success to scope any contract/ops changes. I attached our Redwood BAA eligibility checklist for reference (redwood-baa-eligibility-checklist.pdf).

Available for a call tomorrow between 10–12 PT.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@mediq-analytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Dr. Priya Sharma <priya@mediq-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T14:21:00Z
Subject: Re: BAA question — tokenized EHR snippets + analytics

Thanks Soojin — quick answers inline.

> Can you confirm that no mapping or re-identification keys are ever transmitted to Redwood?
No — mapping table stays in MedIQ systems. We will not send mapping keys. We do, however, plan to keep stable tokens so that we can re-join results to patient records on our side.

> Will derived outputs be re-joined with identifiers on your side?
Yes — counts and features returned from Redwood will be re-joined to our internal patient record to power dashboards and alerts.

> Do you plan to have Redwood use any incoming payloads for fine-tuning?
No — we will not request fine-tuning and we explicitly disallow data reuse in our contract language.

Attached is a redacted sample payload and an updated dataflow (mediq-dataflow-v2.drawio.pdf).

We are hopeful to stay on Hosted for cost reasons, but if Hosted introduces retained logs that contain the stable tokens (and those tokens can be used to re-identify when combined with our mapping), that would be a compliance concern. Can logging be turned off for a specific customer integration, or can you shorten retention to a very small window? Also interested in whether request/response bodies are included in standard telemetry exports (e.g., for ops debugging) and whether Redwood can commit to redacting the token field at rest.

We can do a quick call Thursday 10:30 PT with Marcus and Monica.

—Alex
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@mediq-analytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T16:43:00Z
Subject: Re: BAA question — tokenized EHR snippets + analytics

Alex — thanks for the fast follow and the sample. We reviewed the diagram and the payload you shared; summary and next steps below.

Summary of options (compliance posture):
1) Hosted + BAA (conditional): Possible if all the following hold —
   • You never send mapping keys or re-identification material to Redwood.
   • Tokens are generated using a one-way hash where Redwood cannot derive the original identifier.
   • Redwood's operational logs do not retain the token in cleartext beyond a very short troubleshooting window (we can request a reduced retention policy and configure request-body redaction for your token field).
   • Your contract includes explicit non-reuse and a defined telemetry retention window (we can add an addendum).
   Tradeoffs: lower cost but still some shared-infrastructure risk. We would require an explicit implementation review and a signed BAA addendum.

2) Dedicated: Recommended if you want stronger guarantees around telemetry isolation and the ability to enforce stricter retention at the tenant level. This is our typical recommendation when derived outputs are re-joined to identifiers on your side.

3) Private (VPC/on-prem): For the highest assurance (customer-managed KMS, no Redwood-managed long-term storage).

Specific notes from infra (Marcus):
- By default Hosted logs request/response bodies to support product health and abuse detection. We can implement field-level redaction for the token (server-side) and reduce the retention window to 7 days as part of a contractual change for this integration.
- We cannot commit to completely disabling telemetry for hosted environments due to platform health requirements, but Dedicated can get you to near-zero retained telemetry.

Contract/operational asks from our side:
- Sign the standard BAA and complete the SIG/CAIQ items related to data flow expectations. We can provide a limited BAA addendum for Hosted that lists the redaction/retention commitments.
- Confirmation in writing that MedIQ will not supply mapping keys or request data reuse.

I propose this next sequence:
- Thu 2027-09-16 10:30 PT — 30 min call (Marcus + Monica + Alex + Priya + me) to walk the dataflow and confirm redaction plan.
- MedIQ to sign a BAA and complete the SIG spreadsheet for our review.

I'll attach the SIG starter and the BAA checklist to the thread. If you prefer not to accept any retained telemetry of stable tokens under Hosted, we can scope Dedicated pricing for you.

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sig-questionnaire.xlsx, redwood-baa-eligibility-checklist.pdf
